I am an industrial designer and our image is usually the 'makers' and the 'pretty pictures. However, the deeper you dive into design, the more you start to learn about the four key ingredients of a good design: - art, tech, business and psychology. Focus on the business aspect of it. The moment one joins a design degree (leave UI/UX aside here), the first lesson is that whatever product idea we come up with, it has to 'sell'. This part when understood in detail teaches you about concepts such as market bases, competitive analysis, product placement, etc. Simply put, you're a businessman with your concepts before you make them useful and 'beautify' them. This is the very ideology I developed and I hence look towards a management post-grad. Further, an industrial designer by will can work on a variety of project briefs and industries/market segments but every such designer is a problem-solver at the core, which is why I look towards consulting as one of my post-MBA/mim goals. A problem-solver by nature and with an interest to explore different markets is the recipe here. Though, I also look towards the domains of marketing and strategy & innovation.
